ts-loja-fora-do-ar.enunciado:
We updated the store last night and the site hasn’t opened since. The intern already restarted everything twice, and nothing.

Jorge, who owns the ground-floor shop

Make curl http://loja.local (from your computer, through the Ingress entrance) respond. There’s more than one defect: each fix reveals the next.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.dica: kubectl get pods; kubectl describe pod NAME (Events); kubectl get endpoints loja; kubectl describe svc loja. One defect at a time.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.vidaReal: The store won’t open, and the problem could be in the merchandise (the image), in the clerk (the probe) or in the phone extension (the Service): the building manager checks them one by one, from the stockroom to the front desk.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.limite: At a real store, you can see the counter is closed. In the cluster, each layer fails silently: only the events, the endpoints and describe tell you what’s going on.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.comoSaber: curl http://loja.local returns the store’s JSON, with all 3 replicas ready.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.relato: We updated the store last night and the site hasn’t opened since. The intern already restarted everything twice, and nothing.
ts-loja-fora-do-ar.morador: Jorge, who owns the ground-floor shop

ts-ninguem-se-acha.enunciado:
Since last night’s cleanup, nothing can find anything: the vitrine (storefront) can’t find the estoque (stockroom), and even the caretaker’s test pod says “bad address.” The cleanup crew swears they only turned off what wasn’t being used.

Célia, from the stockroom

Get the pods finding Services by name again: cliente (in default) and vitrine (in the loja namespace) need to call http://estoque.estoque. The store’s turnstile must keep blocking everything else.
ts-ninguem-se-acha.dica: When everything fails at once, look at what everyone uses: kubectl get deploy -n kube-system. Then, if vitrine still can’t find it: kubectl get networkpolicy -n loja.
ts-ninguem-se-acha.vidaReal: The condo’s switchboard operator (CoreDNS) was let go in the cleanup: nobody can get anybody’s number. And in the store’s block, the turnstile only lets people through to the stockroom, and forgot to let them call the switchboard operator.
ts-ninguem-se-acha.limite: Without the switchboard operator, anyone who knows the IP by heart can still call: DNS isn’t the network, it’s just the phone book.
ts-ninguem-se-acha.comoSaber: From both pods, wget -qO- http://estoque.estoque responds; from vitrine, http://admin.default stays blocked.
ts-ninguem-se-acha.relato:
Since last night’s cleanup, nothing can find anything: the vitrine (storefront) can’t find the estoque (stockroom), and even the caretaker’s test pod says
             “bad address.” The cleanup crew swears they only turned off what wasn’t being used.

msgs.3: the store’s turnstile still blocks everything else

ts-fila-parada.enunciado:
The monthly report hasn’t run since yesterday’s maintenance. The maintenance crew said they were done and left. Oh, and just to be safe, I increased the memory the report asks for.

Lima, from finance

Get both replicas of relatorio running. The node maintenance is over: put the nodes back in service (no working around it with tolerations).
ts-fila-parada.dica: kubectl describe pod NAME (the scheduler’s message changes with each fix); kubectl get nodes; kubectl describe node node-2 (Taints). To remove a taint: kubectl taint nodes NODE key=value:Effect- (with the hyphen at the end).
ts-fila-parada.vidaReal: The reports are waiting at the front gate: one building still has tape across its door, the other has the “under renovation” sign, and the request says each report needs a whole floor (300Gi) instead of a room (300Mi).
ts-fila-parada.limite: The doorman explains everything at once. The scheduler also lists the reason for each node, but a node blocked by the tape doesn’t even get measured: the next reason only shows up after the first fix.
ts-fila-parada.comoSaber: Both replicas of relatorio running, and no node closed off or with the maintenance sign.
ts-fila-parada.relato:
The monthly report hasn’t run since yesterday’s maintenance. The maintenance crew said they were done and left.
             Oh, and just to be safe, I increased the memory the report asks for.

msgs.2: node-2 no longer has the maintenance sign
